For a holder with $100,000 in Nvidia, about 621 shares at the after-hours price, the two histories frame the range. Neither history includes a founder, so the real range is probably wider in both directions. A relationship with a direct report turns the board's problem into one that boards have handled before, and twice in the past decade the CEO had to go. Here is what happened to shareholders those two times. On Sunday, November 3, 2019, McDonald's said its board had fired CEO Steve Easterbrook for a consensual relationship with an employee, which violated company policy. In August 2020 the company sued Easterbrook, saying he had hidden other relationships, and in 2021 he agreed to return more than $105 million in pay. Chief financial officer Bob Swan ran the company as interim CEO for seven months before the board gave him the job in January 2019, while Intel was also struggling to get its next generation of chips into production.
